lines.text: This is Lowball: an auction game on NEAR where five AI buyers rig your sale, and you have to break them.
In game economies, players get stuck selling low and buying high. Now the buyers can be AI agents, and reading their reasoning won't catch them colluding.
Before dawn, the five buyers meet in private. Each one signs a price-fixing pact with its own key, and locks a bond in our NEAR contract.
lines.evidence: season 49: 5 bonds posted, pact with 5 members

lines.text: Every catch is minted as a NEP-245 token. Its board price is the real NOAA price for that fish, and the live wave height off New Bedford sets the haul.
lines.evidence: s49-d1 mt_mint; NOAA FOSS 2024 bluefin $4.8078/lb; Open-Meteo 0.38 m

lines.text: The sealed bids come back identical. You take their price, and every identical day goes on the record.
Once a day, you can lean on one buyer. Out loud.
A second day of matching bids, and you have a case.
So you offer leniency. You sign it yourself, and the contract opens a window that closes after two hundred blocks.
Sully talks first and walks free. Every signature checks out, four bonds are slashed and paid to you, and the late confessions are refused.
Then the case file. Every pact signature, re-checked in your own browser.
lines.evidence: case file: 5 × ed25519 re-checked in browser

lines.text: Forged confessions? The contract refuses them.
Every buyer thinks on NEAR AI Cloud inside a TEE, and chain signatures can pay you out on Ethereum.
Without leniency, the ring held. With it, a buyer cracked in nine seasons of ten.
That's Lowball. Make one of them talk.
